- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., > +1.5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.30), model frequently underestimates upward momentum; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; add 1–3% buffer to forecast for volatile sentiment periods.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model tends to lag in recognizing trend reversal; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.
